title: search_logged_models rejects lowercase like/ilike/in operators on SQL stores
answers: logged models filter string lowercase in or ilike fails with Invalid comparison operator
why does search_logged_models only accept uppercase LIKE ILIKE IN
SQL backend logged model filter operator case sensitivity
body:
Symptom: Filtering logged models on a SQL tracking backend with `name like 'x'`, `name ilike 'x'` or `name in (...)` fails with "Invalid comparison operator ... Expected one of ('=', '!=', 'LIKE', 'ILIKE', 'IN', 'NOT IN')".
Root cause: mlflow/utils/search_logged_model_utils.py:parse_filter_string passed the raw operator token to Entity.validate_op and SearchUtils.get_sql_comparison_func, which only accept uppercase forms. Lowercase `not in` worked only because the in-comparison token joiner rewrites it to "NOT IN".
Fix pattern: Normalize the operator token once, right after splitting a comparison into its three non-whitespace tokens and before any validation or lookup (`op = op.upper()`), so every downstream consumer sees the canonical form.
Constraints: Applies to operator handling in parse_filter_string. Keep the normalization before Entity.validate_op. Do not uppercase identifiers or values, which are case-sensitive (names, tag keys, string literals). The test test_search_logged_models_accepts_lowercase_operators in tests/store/tracking/sqlalchemy_store/test_sqlalchemy_store_runs.py covers attributes, params, tags and not in.
applies: Filter-string parsing for search_logged_models; any new operator added to Entity.validate_op must also be recognized in uppercase after this normalization.
says: Searching logged models with lowercase filter operators fails with an invalid comparison error.
Model search filter rejects queries using lowercase pattern matching or list membership conditions.
Filtering logged models by tag or parameter fails when operators are not typed in uppercase.
Allow model search queries to accept lowercase matching keywords without breaking tag case sensitivity.
search: Filter parsing for search_logged_models must normalize comparison operator tokens to uppercase. In mlflow/utils/search_logged_model_utils.py:parse_filter_string, normalize the operator token via op = op.upper() before calling Entity.validate_op and SearchUtils.get_sql_comparison_func on SQL tracking backends. Identifiers and literal values must not be uppercased because attribute names, parameter keys, tag keys, and string literals remain case-sensitive.
